findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted and configured as public with no ACL restricting access, allowing anyone to read or write objects including sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest, risking exposure of sensitive data if underlying storage is compromised.
Versioning is not enabled, meaning objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, which combined with public access increases risk of data tampering or loss.

A customer master data file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer information to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so financial data objects can be overwritten or deleted without the ability to recover previous versions.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational data stored in this bucket is not encrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving data science datasets unencrypted at rest.
